s: In the entertainments of the Vijayanagara kings, apart from Yakshaganam, which art form entertained the common rural people of Andhra?
x:
During the Vijayanagara period, several traditional performing arts flourished under royal patronage. While Yakshaganam was popular in royal courts and among elite audiences, the Leather Puppet Dance (Tholu Bommalata) was the most popular entertainment among the rural population. Tholu Bommalata is a traditional shadow puppet theatre in which colourful leather puppets are manipulated behind a white screen with the help of light. Stories from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas were presented through music, narration and dialogue. This art form served not only as entertainment but also as a medium for religious instruction and moral education. Andhra Pradesh continues to be one of the most important centres of Tholu Bommalata.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).
n: Traditional Shadow Puppet Theatre – Tholu Bommalata

s: A great dancer who performed Kuravanji Dance?
x:
Siddhampuram Kamala was a renowned classical dancer who earned recognition for her outstanding performances of the Kuravanji Dance tradition. Kuravanji is a traditional dance-drama that originated in South India and combines classical dance, music, poetry and dramatic narration. It generally revolves around the story of a heroine seeking union with her beloved, with the fortune-telling Kurathi (tribal woman) playing a central role. Siddhampuram Kamala made significant contributions to preserving and popularizing this traditional art form through her performances and teaching.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Who were Vipravinodulu during the Vijayanagara period?
o: They are a caste of Shudras who depend only on Brahmins for their sustenance.
Shudras performing their arts to entertain Brahmins.
Brahmin jugglers who entertain only Brahmins in their homes.
Brahmin scholars skilled in all arts.
x:
During the Vijayanagara period, Vipravinodulu were Brahmin performers and jugglers who entertained members of the Brahmin community through various magical tricks, acrobatics and amusing performances. The term literally means "those who entertain Brahmins." They formed a distinct professional group and are mentioned in literary works and historical records describing the social life of the Vijayanagara Empire. Their performances were generally confined to Brahmin households and religious gatherings.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Who is known as the "Father of Harikatha"?
x:
Adibhatla Narayana Dasu is popularly known as the "Father of Harikatha" in Telugu. He revolutionized Harikatha by combining music, storytelling, dance, philosophy and literature into a single performance. A multilingual scholar and musician, he played a major role in popularizing this unique performing art throughout Andhra Pradesh.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
n: Father of Harikatha – Adibhatla Narayana Dasu
